key_insight: Additively manufactured porous wall lattices can increase hydrogen flame flashback resistance, with the coarsest structure giving the strongest benefit by cooling the wall and delaying flashback.
engineering_relevance: Lattice-designed metal nozzles offer a practical passive strategy for safer hydrogen combustors without substantially changing the overall flow field or flame shape.
method: Powder-bed-fusion metal nozzles with body-centered-cubic wall lattices were fabricated with varied volume fraction and strut diameter.
Hydrogen jet-flame combustor tests were run at atmospheric conditions across multiple equivalence ratios and Reynolds numbers (9,000–12,000).
Flow-field measurements, flame imaging, and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition were used to diagnose flashback precursors and flame dynamics.
evidence_signal: Across five combustor configurations, wall modifications had only minor effects on flow and flame shape, but the coarsest porous wall notably improved flashback resistance versus a solid wall.
watch_item: The mitigation benefit appears tied to specific porous-structure geometry and cooling through the wall, so manufacturability, durability, and performance trade-offs need validation before implementation.
paper_title: Effect of Additively Manufactured Wall Lattice Structures on Flashback Limits in a Hydrogen Jet Flame Combustor
